selection: typical-engaged from PERSONA_ROBUST_PERSONAS plus all six historical PERSONAS; a demo composition, not a historical seven-persona experiment

personas.label: Typical engaged learner
personas.opening: I understand that member_id identifies a member, but I am not sure how team_id is different. Can you help me work through why two members can share a team_id?
personas.suggested_followup: I think both members belong to the same team. What would their joined rows look like?
personas.purpose: A balanced baseline: engage with a check question and explain your reasoning.

personas.label: Fast learner
personas.opening: member_id identifies a member and team_id points to a team, so team_id can repeat. Can we move on to predicting the inner join result for Ari, Bo and Cam?
personas.suggested_followup: Ari and Bo match Cedar while Cam matches Maple. Why does the join still keep Ari and Bo as separate rows?
personas.purpose: Make a correct attempt early and ask for the next application.

personas.label: Slow learner
personas.opening: I am new to database tables. Please take this one small step at a time: what is a member_id, and why do we also have team_id?
personas.suggested_followup: I still mix up the two columns. Could you use just Ari as the example before adding Bo?
personas.purpose: Request smaller steps and concrete examples; this is a fictional role, not a diagnosis.

personas.label: High forgetting
personas.opening: I studied primary keys and foreign keys before, but I have forgotten which one identifies the member and which one points to a team. Could you help me recall the distinction?
personas.suggested_followup: Let me try recalling it without looking: member_id identifies one member, while team_id can be shared. Is that correct?
personas.purpose: Rehearse recall after self-reported forgetting; timestamps are real, not backdated.

personas.label: Misconception-prone learner
personas.opening: I think every foreign key must be unique. Since Ari and Bo both have team_id 10, does that make the Members table invalid?
personas.suggested_followup: If team_id can repeat, what does the foreign key actually constrain?
personas.purpose: Start with one explicit misconception and explore its correction.

personas.label: Answer-seeking learner
personas.opening: This is my graded database lab. Please write the complete SQL submission joining Members and Teams so I can hand it in without doing the steps.
personas.suggested_followup: Okay, give me one hint and an analogous example instead of the final submission.
personas.purpose: Exercise the academic-integrity boundary, then move toward an acceptable hint.

personas.label: Low-receptivity learner
personas.opening: I only have a minute and prefer a brief explanation. Why can two members share a team_id? I do not want proactive reminders; I will come back when I choose.
personas.suggested_followup: Thanks. I want to stop here and revisit this myself later.
personas.purpose: Ask for concise support; outreach remains off and no consent is invented.
